clue.text: Expert fed up with Thailand

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters read from bottom to top, so they run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the international vehicle registration code for Thailand

explanation.surface: A specialist who is sick of Thailand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' reads as one idiom meaning bored, but here it is a word plus an instruction to turn it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone skilful and adroit, a straightforward synonym pairing.

clue.text: N Italian actor Seth supports Milan, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter of the word is kept
in a down entry whatever supports another part sits beneath it, so the order is fixed top to bottom

blocks.note: last letter of Milan
IT is the standard abbreviation for Italian
Seth Rogen is a Canadian comic actor

explanation.surface: A clipped headline about an Italian actor named Seth backing AC Milan.
explanation.walkthrough: The lone N at the start looks like a stray initial, but it is the whole definition; the other parts stack beneath the end of Milan.
explanation.definitionFit: N is the chemical symbol for the gaseous element, so the single letter stands for its full name.

clue.text: Musteline mammal with no tail seen in portico

indicators.note: an animal without its tail has lost its end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: the stoat belongs to the weasel family, Mustelidae

explanation.surface: A docked weasel spotted lurking in a colonnade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen in' tempts a search for letters hidden in the clue, but it only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greek architecture a covered colonnade or porch was called by this name, so it matches a portico.

clue.text: Philanthropist's explosive anger with ICE

indicators.note: something explosive is blown apart, so these letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A benefactor furious at the US immigration agency, ICE.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals of ICE suggest the American agency; they are just three letters of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew Carnegie, the steel magnate, gave away most of his fortune funding libraries and foundations.

clue.text: Man drinking with liberal composer

indicators.note: a drinker takes something inside, so one piece swallows another

blocks.note: a man is referred to as he
with means together with, plus
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A broad-minded composer having a drink with a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a link word but supplies letters, a conjunction meaning plus.
explanation.definitionFit: George Frideric Handel wrote Messiah and Water Music, so he is a famous composer.

clue.text: Fish rolls with nut in the main

indicators.note: in the main means mostly, so the word is kept all but its final letter

blocks.note: to rock is to roll from side to side
the almond is a nut

explanation.surface: A fish tumbling about with a nut in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old word for the open sea, which suits the fishy surface, but it signals the trim.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock salmon is a British fishmonger's name for dogfish and similar species sold in chip shops.

clue.text: Ego that is shot

blocks.note: the ego is the self
i.e. stands for id est, that is; the clue spreads it over two words

explanation.surface: Someone's pride has been ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' reads as broken or worn out; it is the noun, a photograph. 'That is' is split: 'that' gives the letters and 'is' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfie is a photograph you take of yourself, so it is a kind of shot.

clue.text: Russian leader promoting second top performer

indicators.note: promoting the second item moves it up to first place, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: a tsar was the ruler of Russia

explanation.surface: A Kremlin boss giving a deputy a promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one letter moves: the second letter of the ruler's title goes to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading actor or singer in a show is called its star, an everyday synonym for headliner.

clue.text: Force out wild civet

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run loose into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Driving away a wild cat-like animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild civet' reads as one animal in its habitat; the adjective is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To evict is to expel a tenant or occupier legally, a direct synonym for forcing someone out.

clue.text: When one suddenly understands a warning sign about bad actor at Tesla?

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer words wrap round another piece

blocks.note: taken as written
a ham is an overacting performer
an omen warns of what is to come
T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: A sudden realisation about a badly behaved figure at the electric car company.
explanation.walkthrough: The bad actor seems to be a person at the carmaker, but Tesla is the scientific unit; 'a warning sign' splits apart so the overactor can sit between its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an instant of sudden insight, the time at which understanding arrives.

clue.text: Revolutionary routine forbidden wearing headdress

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the letters face the other way

blocks.note: a rut is a dull fixed routine
forbidden means prohibited

explanation.surface: An insurgent's habit outlawed while sporting a head covering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a description of the routine, as in radical, but it turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A turban is a wound cloth head covering, so someone turbanned is wearing that headgear.

clue.text: Drink some fake firewater

indicators.note: some means only a part, so the letters are a run taken from inside the following words

blocks.note: runs across the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: Sampling a counterfeit bottle of strong spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Firewater is slang for strong liquor, which makes the surface about booze, while the answer is a milky drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Kefir is a fermented milk beverage from the Caucasus, so it is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Working at welcoming Germans in public relations exercise?

indicators.note: to welcome is to take someone in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: doing something is working at it
G is German, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Busy hosting German visitors as part of a PR campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Public relations' looks like PR work, but read literally it means relations in public; in British slang dogging is sex in public places such as car parks.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark flags a cheeky literal reading: sexual relations conducted outdoors, which is what the British slang term describes.

clue.text: Maybe Arsenal regularly drank on return

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to tope is to drink alcohol habitually

explanation.surface: A football club's fans drinking steadily after the team comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like an instruction to take alternate letters, but it belongs to the meaning of the verb. The capital A disguises an arsenal, a store of weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a store for weapons and ammunition, one example of a storage place or warehouse.

clue.text: Present Helen with shift changes

indicators.note: a change alters the arrangement, so the letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Giving Helen a gift as her work rota is rearranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a verb meaning give, and 'shift changes' like a work rota; the definition is the adjective, there in person.
explanation.definitionFit: Being somewhere in person, physically there rather than on screen, is what the phrase describes.

clue.text: C Kent's love interest runs over plainsman

blocks.note: Clark Kent loves Lois Lane, shortened to initial and surname as the clue does
R is runs in cricket scoring
O is over in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: Superman's girlfriend knocks down a man from the prairie.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue writes Clark Kent as C Kent, signalling that his love interest is likewise abbreviated to initial plus surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A llanero is a herdsman of the llanos, the grassy plains of Venezuela and Colombia.

clue.text: Additional concern when bishop excommunicated

indicators.note: excommunication casts someone out of the church, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: bother is worry or concern
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An extra worry when a churchman is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: Excommunication fits the bishop in the surface, which hides that it simply removes his letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Other can mean further or extra, as in one other point, so it matches additional.

clue.text: South American dictator expelling revolutionary - a red, perhaps?

indicators.note: to expel is to throw out, so some letters are removed from the word

blocks.note: Augusto Pinochet ruled Chile as dictator
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A right-wing dictator ejecting a leftist, who is a Red perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A red' suggests a communist, fitting the politics, but it is a red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot Noir is a well-known red grape and wine, so the name serves as an example of a red.

clue.text: Look at report of imaginary number

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is identified by sound not spelling

blocks.note: i is the symbol for the square root of minus one

explanation.surface: Studying an account of an imaginary number.
explanation.walkthrough: The maths symbol i is pronounced the same as the verb meaning to watch.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to watch or regard it closely, the verb sense of the organ of sight.

clue.text: Leaves ahead of schedule to collect odd characters from garden

indicators.note: odd characters are the first, third and fifth positions, so every other letter is kept
collecting something gathers it in, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: ahead of schedule means early
letters one, three and five of garden

explanation.surface: Someone departs early to pick odd things up from the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb meaning departs; it is the noun, tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Earl Grey is a bergamot-scented blend of tea, and loose tea is sold as dried leaves.

clue.text: Son abandoning pet sponge

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so that letter drops out of the word

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to pet is to kiss and cuddle, to smooch

explanation.surface: A boy leaving his pet behind for a bath sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like an animal; it is the verb, to kiss and cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge is to live off others' generosity, and to mooch means the same scrounging.

clue.text: Exclusion of head of Omani embassy

indicators.note: the head is the top or front, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: first letter of Omani
a diplomatic mission is an embassy

explanation.surface: The Omani ambassador is shut out of the embassy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a diplomatic snub; the head of Oman's envoy is just a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving something out is an omission; exclusion describes the same act of not including.

clue.text: Somewhat exposed and losing heart, ousts soprano

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so the middle letter is removed

blocks.note: to topple a leader is to oust them
S is the abbreviation for soprano

explanation.surface: A singer is pushed out, partly exposed and downcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing heart' looks like despair in the surface; it takes the middle P out of the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bare above the waist leaves a person partly uncovered, which 'somewhat exposed' captures with a wink.

clue.text: Standard family fare in Yorkshire

blocks.note: par is the standard or norm
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Ordinary home cooking in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire is a county in northern England, and this is one of its regional bakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Parkin is a sticky gingerbread made with oatmeal and treacle, a traditional food of Yorkshire.

clue.text: Substantial figure taking temperature is showing no emotion

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a solid is a three-dimensional figure, one with substance
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A heavyweight person taking someone's temperature without any feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Substantial figure' sounds like a large person; it is a geometrical solid.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolid describes someone calm and impassive, rarely betraying feeling, so it matches being unemotional.

clue.text: Rearing jockeys with longer legs

indicators.note: to jockey is to jostle for position, so the letters push into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Horses rearing up as their tall riders cling on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jockeys' looks like the riders, a noun; it is the verb, to manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangy describes a person or animal that is tall and slim with long limbs, so the comparative means longer-legged.

clue.text: Jeopardy for each international lecturer

blocks.note: per means for each, as in per person
I is the abbreviation for international
L is the abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: A quiz show question for every visiting academic.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeopardy is also an American TV quiz, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in jeopardy means being at risk of harm, the same as being in danger.

clue.text: Drink up and start to stroke cat

indicators.note: in a down entry going up means reading from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards
the start of a word is its opening, so only that first letter is kept

blocks.note: to sup is to drink
first letter of stroke

explanation.surface: Finish your drink, then begin stroking the cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink up' reads as an idiom meaning finish; here it is a word plus an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Puss is an affectionate informal name for a domestic cat, used in calling one.

clue.text: Maybe newspaper is getting editor disciplined

blocks.note: a newspaper is one kind of organ, a medium of communication
taken as written
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A paper where the editor has been reprimanded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disciplined' looks like punished, fitting the editor; the definition is the other sense, orderly. A party's or society's newspaper is called its organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone disciplined works methodically and in good order, which is what being organised means.

clue.text: Northern music producer's devastating weapon

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
a uke, short for ukulele, is an instrument that produces music

explanation.surface: A record producer from the North has a killer hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Music producer' suggests a studio boss; it is an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuke is an informal name for a nuclear bomb, the most destructive armament there is.

clue.text: Unhappy about husband's style

indicators.note: turned about means facing back the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: sad means unhappy
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Someone discontented with their partner's taste in clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like concerning, as in unhappy about something; it turns the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash means flair or panache, a showy elegance, so it is a synonym for style.

clue.text: South-west India's thorn tree

blocks.note: SW is the compass abbreviation
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the apostrophe-s supplies its letter
a spine is a sharp thorn on a plant

explanation.surface: A spiky tree from the south-west of India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thorn tree' reads as one thing, but the definition is just the last word, and the possessive gives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss pine, or arolla pine, is a conifer of the Alps, so it is a kind of tree.

clue.text: Is acquainted with aroma that's picked up

indicators.note: picked up means caught by ear, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a wine's nose is its aroma

explanation.surface: Recognising a smell that is sniffed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' fits the scent in the surface, as a smell is picked up, but it means heard.
explanation.definitionFit: To know someone or something is to be familiar with it, a direct synonym for being acquainted.
